note: Peekaboo picks: which central-catalogue records the webapp shows and the few words it adds to each. Records tagged 'peekaboo' (scope.tags) are picked up automatically; ids listed under 'ids' are added by hand. 'said' is what the label, catalogue or reply stated; 'found' is what was there. Facts and dates only. — Cedwyn editors

OBS-PEEKABOO-NEWMAN-IA.category: Catalogue description does not match the item
OBS-PEEKABOO-NEWMAN-IA.said: The catalogue description of the Internet Archive copy: “A very hairy but not-too-scary monster story. One dark, stormy night, Owl, Mouse and Rabbit are afraid. Could it be the Monster of the Woods knocking at the door?”
OBS-PEEKABOO-NEWMAN-IA.found: The item is John Newman’s Glamorgan (The Buildings of Wales, 1995), a 717-page architectural guide with entries for Llandough-juxta-Penarth (pp.378–379), Leckwith (pp.370–371) and Cogan.
OBS-PEEKABOO-NEWMAN-IA.why: The summary note belongs to a children’s picture book. Searched by its description, the guide would not be found.

OBS-PEEKABOO-DBDT79-CATALOGUE.said: Catalogue entry: “Lease (counterpart) of land and premises situate in Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff, from the Marquess of Bute to Mr John Williams, May 1877.”
OBS-PEEKABOO-DBDT79-CATALOGUE.found: Examined at our request, the original is a counterpart lease of 2 May 1877 from the Trustees of the Will of the late Marquess of Bute to Mr John Williams of Newport. Glamorgan Archives: “The catalogue description for DBDT/79/1 had a few small errors which have now been corrected.”
OBS-PEEKABOO-DBDT79-CATALOGUE.why: A physical check of the original, asked for on 26 August 2026, found the catalogue wording wrong. The deed concerns Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff; the archive found no mention of Llandough in it.

TOC-F05.said: Cadw, 25 February 2026: “much of the content in your correspondence falls outside the scope of Cadw’s work.”
TOC-F05.found: Cadw, 21 May 2026: its electronic records held the 1988 listing assessment of Great House Farm and Barn, and two photographs dated 29 July 1988.
TOC-F05.why: The records were in Cadw’s own system; they came out once a request named the property and the 1988 survey.

TOC-F01.said: Amgueddfa Cymru – Museum Wales, 25 August 2026: “Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold the requested information.”
TOC-F01.found: Museum Wales, 22 September 2026: records of archaeological discoveries recorded at Great House Farm and Church Farm, Llandough, identified in the searches for the first request.
TOC-F01.why: The records were found in the first search and set aside as outside its scope; they were released four weeks later on a fresh request.

TOC-F02.said: Historic England, 21 October 2026: “we do not hold any information that falls within the scope of your request.”
TOC-F02.found: Historic England, 27 October 2026: a letter of transfer to RCAHMW dated 12 January 2018.
TOC-F02.why: The first reply itself recorded the 12 January 2018 transfer; the covering letter followed six days after a challenge.

TOC-F03.said: Vale of Glamorgan Council, 2 June 2026: “the Vale of Glamorgan Council does not hold records relating to this historic legal matter.”
TOC-F03.found: Vale of Glamorgan Council, 11 September 2026: “further historical documentation has been found.” Not yet disclosed.
TOC-F03.why: Found once service areas were asked again; the council is still sifting it.
